steps.text: Preheat oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C). Grease one 8x8 inch pan.
In a large bowl, mix together the rolled oats and butter. Mix in boiling water. Set aside to cool.
Beat together the brown sugar, eggs and vanilla; add to cooled oat mixture and mix well.
Sift together the flour, baking soda, baking powder, salt and cocoa. Add to wet ingredients and mix well. Spread into the prepared pan.
Bake at 350 degrees F (175 degrees C) for 40 minutes. Remove from oven, allow to cool, and remove pan.

raw_recipe.headline: Chocolate Oatmeal Cake
raw_recipe.description: The butter and cocoa give this wholesome cake a fudgey quality, while the oatmeal adds fiber and density.
raw_recipe.name: Chocolate Oatmeal Cake

recipeInstructions.text: Preheat oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C). Grease one 8x8 inch pan.
In a large bowl, mix together the rolled oats and butter. Mix in boiling water. Set aside to cool.
Beat together the brown sugar, eggs and vanilla; add to cooled oat mixture and mix well.
Sift together the flour, baking soda, baking powder, salt and cocoa. Add to wet ingredients and mix well. Spread into the prepared pan.
Bake at 350 degrees F (175 degrees C) for 40 minutes. Remove from oven, allow to cool, and remove pan.

review.reviewBody: Very nice recipe, however I did make some changes. First, I was running low on brown sugar, so I used 3/4 cup brown, and 3/4 cup white. Then, I added WAY more coco powder then called for. (Probably about 1/2 cup) It turned our great! SOOOO chocolatly and rich. It was great just like that. Didn't even need any icing. :)

The chocolate cake was yummy, very moist. I substituted Oat flour for all-purpose and added 1 Tblsp. Chia seeds. The frosting is Easy Peanut Butter frosting from Allrecipes. It was a fast birthday cake without having too much leftover. 

Great fast snack cake with or without frosting.

I've made this as-is and thought it was just ok. I actually hybridized this recipe and the BC Oatmeal Applesauce Cake recipe and it is fantastic!! 1 full cup oatmeal, 3/4-1 cup applesauce and enough apple juice to measure 1 and 1/4 cup liquid, 1/4 cup chocolate syrup, and a full 1/2 cup cocoa powder and then the rest of the listed flour, baking soda, eggs, butter, etc listed in this recipe.
Sometimes I top with nuts or chocolate icing, sometimes I leave it plain.

Very good, I read the reviews, but did not have applesauce, so I used two mashed banana's in place of the butter. I also added the extra vanilla and cinnamon that everyone mentioned. I used coconut oil to grease the pan. I was looking for a coconut topping to bake on top. Next time. I will make it again.

Delicious! Moist and easy. I used 1/4 cup apple sauce 1/4 butter, 1 egg 1 egg white, and subbed splenda for half of the sugar. I also used 1/2 cup of cocoa. I didn't add frosting, but cream cheese frosting would be delicious!
Substituted the water for black coffee and cut the brown sugar to 1 cup. So delicious and moist.

I made this cake yesterday. I added an extra tablespoon of cocoa powder and still found that the cake didnt have enough flavour. If it was more chocolately it would have been a really nice cake. I will try making it again adding more cocoa and maybe choc chips. UPDATE.. Made cake again using 4 tablespoons plus half cup of cocoa powder and added 1 tsp on cinnamon. I also swapped the butter for applesauce. YUM. Will make again.

Chocolatey (used about 1/2 cup cocoa) and yummy. Feels a little good for you too - used about 1/3 cup applesauce in place of 1/3 cup of butter and added butter to make the difference to equal 1/2 cup. Thanks for sharing.
I substituted applesauce for butter, added 1 tsp of cinnamon, and used 1/4 c of dark chocolate cocoa as other reviewers suggested. Excellent!

SERIOUSLY the best cake ever! I used 1/2 cup Cocoa powder and 2 tsp of vanilla instead of 1. The flavor and texture was amazing! So moist and chewy. LOVED the oatmeal in it - it gives it the best texture. I made a Chocolate Ganache to go on top and it was great. My husband who doesn't eat chocolate or dessert had two pieces saying it was by far the best chocolate cake I have ever made! I will be using this recipe again and again for a long time!
For less caloric intake I used coconut oil in place of the butter, whole wheat flour, and only 1 cup of brown sugar. It still tasted sweet and I felt less guilty about it! Delicious recipe.
Family favorite. Very moist and rich. We usually double the recipe.
Turned out perfectly! Made whipped cream to go on top. Very moist, good flavor!
Added more cocoa powder and cinnamon as others suggested. This is a quick cake to make and was tasty. I liked the oatmeal texture.

Most amazing and tastiest cake I have ever made! I followed the receipe n it turned out brilliant! Dense dark chocolate colour, all over moist n super soft! 
Vanished before I could take picture!!!
I enjoy subtle cakes, however, my dessert loving family didn't. Add frosting maybe? Good with a cup of joe.
I had to bake this for 55 min. in a 8x8..super moist and i did add more coco.
Good tasting recipe. Easy to prepare and the results were yummy. My results tasted more like brownie than cake. Not complaining, just stating. Everyone still cobbled it up!
Must have done something wrong. Oatmeal came out almost hard & chewy. Lacked flavor. Comes out of my recipe box!

I tried this recipe and it was just okay, I will not being making this again because it had no taste. I did not mind the chewy taste of the oatmeal because I love it, but when adding the chocolate it did not help with the taste and I added cinnamon and I think for that 1/2 cup of butter may have taken the taste away, to much. but it was just okay.
